teaser.text: Applied Materials sells the machines that chipmakers use to build chips, rather than making the finished chips itself. Its dollar comes in through equipment sales and continuing services, after going out first on engineering, components, manufacturing, delivery, and support.

blocks.heading: What has to go right—and wrong for Applied Materials?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives operating profit of $9,570 million, $8,525 million and $9,860 million as revenue falls, utilization weakens and operating leverage bites. The bull case gives $12,480 million, $14,256 million and $15,840 million as AI, DRAM, packaging and leading-edge investment become repeat orders. Q3 DRAM growth was 52%, and foundry-and-logic revenue reached a record, supporting the upside but not proving a full-cycle result.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Applied Materials really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow records money collected from customers after cash payments to employees, suppliers and governments. Free cash flow then subtracts capital spending on facilities and equipment. A stricter measure also subtracts stock compensation, because employees receive ownership with economic value even though the award requires no immediate cash payment.

The sensible measure is therefore a multi-year cash record. Average free cash flow across 2021–2025 is useful, but it still combines different demand conditions and investment stages. Applied has not disclosed enough to separate maintenance spending from expansion spending, so sustainable cash generation remains an estimate.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Applied Materials today?

paragraphs.text: Revenue growth slowed from 34.1% in FY2021 to 4.4% in FY2025, while operating margin stayed near 29%–30%. Applied’s computed free cash flow—cash from operations minus capital spending—fell as a share of revenue in FY2025. Real free cash flow per share fell while diluted EPS held up. At $507.03 a share, trailing P/E is 43.7x and next-twelve-month P/E is 27.1x. Free cash flow yield is 1.4%; dividend yield is 0.4%. Buybacks reduced the share count but cannot replace cash generation.

blocks.heading: Is Applied Materials' dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Across fiscal 2021–2025, Applied generated US$30,165 million of free cash flow and paid shareholders US$26,022 million. Free cash flow is the operating cash left after capital spending, so this distribution came after research, buildings and equipment had already consumed cash.

The annual pattern was less even. In fiscal 2022, Applied paid shareholders US$6,976 million against US$4,612 million of free cash flow. In fiscal 2025, it paid US$6,279 million against US$5,698 million generated. Such payouts can draw on saved cash or borrowing, but repeated excess distributions reduce the financial cushion. Applied ended fiscal 2025 with US$2,018 million of net cash, down from US$3,212 million a year earlier.

earnings.closing: The full Applied Materials memo also answers how the business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the path.

blocks.heading: What has Applied Materials guided for Q4 FY2026?

paragraphs.text: From $507.03, the weighted forecast points to losses through October 2029 as multiple compression outweighs operating growth; it hinges on durable AI-led demand, production wins and cash generation. Management guides Q4 FY2026 revenue to $9,750–$10,750 million. Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance is $3.82–$4.22. Packaging revenue is expected to grow more than 70% in calendar 2026, with AGS revenue growing 20%.

blocks.heading: Has Applied Materials kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management has kept some promises: Applied reported six consecutive years of revenue growth, and record third-quarter revenue in August 2026 supported its demand outlook. But EPIC began installation and operations later than its original early-2026 target, and the promised 80–100% distribution of free cash flow must be judged over several years. Management’s incentives point toward shareholders; spending discipline and execution will decide whether that alignment is real.

blocks.heading: What do Applied Materials' last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, gross margin and operating income all strengthened, and operating expenses grew more slowly than sales. Across the recent quarters, the sequence supports a recovery rather than a single isolated spike.

Reported net income fell from April even though operating profit rose. April included a $685 million strategic-investment gain, while July included a $220 million expense. Removing the July unrealized loss alone brings reported EPS closer to the company’s adjusted result. The lesson is simple: investment marks can overwhelm the operating signal in any single quarter.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Applied Materials' next results?

paragraphs.text: Applied scheduled EPIC’s unveiling for **October 12, 2026**, followed by an investor presentation on October 13. The useful evidence will be operating tools, active joint development and progress toward customer qualification. More partners broaden the opportunity, but qualification will show whether the center is shortening the path from research to equipment sales.
